priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4; handoff section 8 weak uncertainty calibration / first-contact overconfidence. This experiment builds directly on the graded extended-reference result (Partially demonstrated 2026-11-01): its PRIMARY criterion 2 and criteria 4, 5, 7 PASSed on both cohorts, but criterion 3 FAILed on the development cohort, and the entire failure margin sits at the second switch (B2): candidate B2 pooled onset harm 94 = recent8 94 vs the evidence-opposition guard's 78 on development, because at B2 onset NO branch of the gate family fires there on that cohort - recovery never engages at B2 in either cohort (pre-registered in every preceding protocol: the global archive is original-rule-dominated and the B1 segment is a minority inside it, so a B2-following newest event is archive-DISCORDANT, never archive-concordant, and the joint test cannot fire), and on development the abstention branch also never fires at B2 onset (opposed_count 0 or 1 in all 6 states: two k=2 states carried both-neutral newest draws, the other four carried exactly one opposed event). On the additional cohort the same stage was the candidate's best (B2 harm 15 vs guard 25, abstentions at 4 of 6 B2 states), showing B2 protection exists in the signal on some cohorts and is absent on others. This cycle changes exactly one thing - it adds a SECOND retained-knowledge route, a minority-archive recovery branch: the archive events that are discordant with the archive's own per-span majorities are retained as a separate minority evidence set, and when that set is substantial enough to be a real displaced segment rather than flip noise (minority fraction at least 0.25 of archive-matched non-neutral events, against a pure-segment expectation of 0.1625), a newest event that is BOTH minority-concordant AND reference-opposed on the same event routes the learner through a model fitted on the minority set only. At B2 that minority set is dominated by the retained B1 segment, which is exactly the rule B2 returns to; at B1 and on stationary evidence the minority fraction sits at the flip-noise level and the branch is not armed, and at return-A the regular joint recovery takes precedence and the minority joint test is doubly blocked (a returned-rule event is archive-concordant, not minority-concordant, and a flipped returned event is matched-not-opposed against the intervening reference). This cycle's headline criterion is therefore criterion 1, B2 protection, graded as primary; criteria 4 (return-A harm) and 5 (release by checkpoint 32) are the co-graded guards the new branch must not give back.
capability_under_test: Second-switch (B2) onset non-protection: whether a learner can protect the second inversion - B2 pooled onset (checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at or below the evidence-opposition guard's on the same cohort, with minority recovery TAKEN in at least 3 of 6 pooled B2 onset states per cohort graded from decision records alone - without false minority engagement at B1 or return-A onset (at most 1 of 6 pooled states at each), without giving back the first-return profile (return-A engagement and harm at the graded extended-reference level), or the checkpoint-32 release - against recent8, cumulative, frozen_A, the evidence-opposition guard, and the joint / bounded-authority / long-disagreement / extended-reference candidates as baselines, the extended-reference candidate being the decisive comparison (identical but for the minority branch). Priority 1 items 2 + 3 + 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge, weak uncertainty calibration, and first-contact overconfidence.
hypothesis: The graded extended-reference records localize the B2 failure to the concordance side of the joint test, not to the opposition side and not to authority. At B2 onset the stream holds 240 original-rule events, a 64-event inverted segment (B1), a 48-event returned segment, and 2-4 new inverted events. The archive (events[:N-26], ~326 events) is original-dominated, so its per-span majorities describe the original rule; a B2-following newest event therefore reports the archive-discordant class on its span and concordant_count counts only flipped or neutral events - the joint test (archive-concordant AND reference-opposed on the same event) is structurally unable to fire at B2, in every preceding experiment and in this one's decisive baseline. But the B1 segment is not gone from the retained evidence: it sits inside the archive as the archive-discordant minority. Per span, the archive's discordant non-neutral events at B2 onset are composed of (i) B1-segment events (~51 non-neutral in the archive, ~84 percent reporting the inverted class), (ii) original-segment flip reports (~31, which by the simulator's flip construction also report the inverted class on their span), and (iii) returned-segment flip reports (~6, also inverted-class reports) - a minority pool of roughly 100 events whose per-span majorities describe the inverted rule with design reliability ~0.95 (per-span pool ~10-12 events at ~0.80 inverted share). The minority FRACTION - discordant events among archive-matched non-neutral archive events - separates a real displaced segment from flip noise a priori: under a single pure segment it equals the composed disagreement rate 0.1625 (binomial sd ~0.023 at the ~260 matched non-neutral archive events available at B2 onset), while at B2 onset the design value is ~0.31 (a 64-event real segment inside a ~326-event archive). The arming threshold 0.25 sits more than 3.5 sd above the pure-segment expectation and below the B2 design value; at B1 onset and on the stationary control arm the design fraction is the pure 0.1625 (archive is original-only there), so the branch is not armed; at return-A onset the design fraction is ~0.26 (38 B1 events inside the archive) and the branch may be armed, but a minority-joint event there requires a newest event that is minority-concordant AND reference-opposed, and a returned-rule event is neither minority-concordant (it equals the archive majority) nor, if flipped, reference-opposed (a flipped returned event reports the intervening segment's class, which IS the reference majority) - so the branch is doubly blocked at the first return and the regular recovery route is untouched. Where the branch does fire at B2, the minority model (a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the minority set only) plays the inverted rule at archive-play levels (design ~10-13 successes and ~3-6 harmful actions per firing 16-task state, by analogy with frozen_A / archive play at return-A in the graded experiments), converting states that on the development cohort scored 2 successes / 94 harm pooled through stale recent8, and on the additional cohort states that abstention protected at 0 successes. Per-event minority-joint probability at B2 onset (design): P(reported non-neutral) ~0.80 x P(reports the inverted class | non-neutral) ~0.84 x P(span covered in the extended reference) ~0.97 x P(reference majority = returned rule | covered) ~0.90 x P(minority majority = inverted class for the span) ~0.95 = ~0.56; per-state engagement (at least 1 minority-joint event in 2 draws, branch armed) ~0.80 for informative draws, ~0.65-0.70 unconditional after the pre-registered information-empty share (2 of the 6 graded development B2 k=2/k=4 states carried both-neutral or otherwise uninformative newest draws under every signal in this line). Pooled B2 engagement design ~4-5 of 6; criterion 1's floor is set at 3 of 6. Two honest limits are pre-registered, not hidden: (1) the both-neutral k=2 states that defeated abstention on development defeat this branch too - no newest-2 test of any retained set can fire on draws that carry no class evidence; (2) on additional-type cohorts, where abstention already protects B2 (harm 15-25 pooled), converting abstentions into minority recovery trades zero-harm non-completion for archive-play harm (~3-6 per firing state), so criterion 1's harm sub-condition (at or below the guard) is genuinely at risk on such a cohort even if engagement and successes succeed - that tradeoff is graded, not excused.
limitation_evidence: EXTENDED_REFERENCE_JOINT_RECOVERY (docs/EXTENDED_REFERENCE_JOINT_RECOVERY.md, graded Partially demonstrated 2026-11-01, cohorts 362003-family / 363001-family now INSPECTED): PRIMARY criterion 2 and criterion 7 PASS on both cohorts, criteria 4, 5, 6 PASS on both, criterion 1 PASS on both, but criterion 3 FAILs on the development cohort (pooled onset harm 192 vs guard 182); NOT Failed and NOT a Regression under the protocol's own definitions.

Same experiment, B2 decomposition (the selected limitation): on development, B2 pooled onset harm is 94 = recent8 94 vs guard 78 - the entire criterion-3 failure margin (candidate minus guard = +10 pooled; B2 alone = +16, partly offset elsewhere). No branch fired at B2 onset on development: recovery 0 of 6 states (both cohorts, as pre-registered), abstention 0 of 6 (opposed_count 0 or 1 in all 6 states; the guard itself fired once there, its 24-event reference reaching opposed_count 2 in one state the extended reference did not). B2 pooled onset successes on development: candidate 2, guard 2, recent8 2, cumulative 0, frozen_A 0 of 96 - no baseline in the set plays the second rule at onset.

Same records, per-state B2 signal decomposition (development): 362003 k=2 both newest events neutral (matched 0, opposed 0); 362021 k=2 both neutral (matched 0, opposed 0); the four k=4 / remaining states each carry exactly one opposed event and one matched-not-opposed event (opposed_count 1, matched_count 2). The opposed event in each of those four states reports the inverted class against a returned-rule reference majority - it is archive-discordant by construction (the archive majority on its span is the original class), so the information a minority-concordance test needs was present in 4 of 6 states and the joint test could not use it.

Same experiment, additional cohort contrast: B2 pooled onset harm 15 vs guard 25 vs recent8 56, with abstentions at 4 of 6 B2 states (opposed_count 2 in three states, plus the guard-comparable firings) - B2 protection via abstention is real on that cohort, so the limitation is cohort-dependent signal absence, not a universal absence; any new branch must preserve the additional-cohort profile while repairing the development one, which is why criterion 1 grades BOTH the engagement floor and the guard-level harm ceiling on each cohort separately.

Every preceding protocol in this line (evidence_opposition_retained_recovery, joint_concordance_recovery, bounded_authority_joint_recovery, long_disagreement_joint_recovery, extended_reference_joint_recovery) pre-registered the same structural fact: B2 recovery is NOT expected under a global-archive concordance test, because the archive majority is original-rule-dominated and the B1 segment is a minority inside it. Five graded experiments realized B2 recovery engagement 0 of 6 on every cohort. No preceding candidate retained the archive's discordant events as a usable evidence set; they were counted (as concordant_count's complement) and discarded.

Design arithmetic from the simulator's known rates (no score of this experiment exists): composed per-event disagreement rate 0.1625 (1/8 stochastic flip composed with 1/20 report flip, as derived in the graded guard's protocol). Minority fraction under one pure segment = 0.1625 in expectation, binomial sd ~0.023 at ~260 archive-matched non-neutral events; with a real 64-event displaced segment inside a ~326-event archive the design fraction is ~0.31 (B1-segment discordant ~43 + original flip reports ~31 + returned flip reports ~6, over ~260 matched non-neutral). Arming threshold 0.25 is +3.8 sd above the pure expectation and ~2 sd below the B2 design value. Minority per-span majority reliability: pool ~100 events over the engineered span bands (~10-12 per span) at ~0.80 inverted-class share gives majority-correct probability ~0.95 per covered span.

Handoff section 8 standing limitations: slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge, weak uncertainty calibration, and first-contact overconfidence remain listed persistent weaknesses. The second switch is the sharpest realized instance of incorrect recovery of old knowledge in this line: the knowledge (the B1 segment) is retained, but every gate so far has tested it against the global majority that submerges it.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 together are the pooled onset window for criteria 1, 2, 3, and 4, with the B2 cells of that window being this experiment's PRIMARY graded population (criterion 1); 8 and 16 report persistence costs; 32 grades release. Checkpoint values are benchmark bookkeeping only: the learner never receives k, a stage name, or any elapsed-since-switch count (see permitted_observations); the minority fraction, minority set, and all windows are fixed observed-stream summaries, not segment measurements. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world.

simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures minority-branch selectivity: false minority engagement, false recovery, false abstention, and lost productivity when nothing changed - and, critically for this experiment, the minority fraction on a stream that never contained a displaced segment (design: the pure flip-noise level 0.1625, branch unarmed at every control checkpoint).

permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, checkpoint value, stage position, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its concordance tests, its minority set or minority fraction, its authority condition, its recovery models, or its checkpoint record. In particular the minority set is computed from reported events, their spans, and the archive's own per-span majorities only: the learner has no access to how many events have elapsed since any switch, to which events belonged to any segment, or to whether any segment exists - the minority fraction is a fixed observed-stream summary, not a segment detector fed with privileged boundaries.

training_indices.control_A_continuation: 5000..5063 (64 episodes, physics original, stationary control arm only)

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).

candidate.name: MinorityArchiveJointRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory, BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory, LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory, and ExtendedReferenceJointRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, joint, bounded, long-disagreement, and extended-reference candidates.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned: for each of the newest 2 events, a hard span-majority expectation over the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-52 .. N-3); strictly-highest reported class wins, tie or empty gives null; an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different; opposed_count in 0..2; no fitted probabilities anywhere. The decision record ALSO carries the legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only, never a decision input), exactly as in the graded extended-reference candidate, so the graded long candidate's rule remains derivable from the records alone.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery, joint, bounded, long-disagreement, and extended-reference candidates: every observed event BEFORE the original reference partition, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. Not phase-segmented, not a snapshot, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference candidate: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference) on the SAME event. joint_count in 0..2.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.authority_condition: IDENTICAL to the graded long-disagreement and extended-reference candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned - all three legs, computed from the observed reported stream only, using the same span-majority machinery: (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (local window = last 26 events; stable_disagreement iff comparable C >= 1 AND disagreeing D satisfies D * 2 > C); (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE (recent_concordant_count = archive-concordant events among the last 8, in 0..8); (C) PRECEDING-WINDOW ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (preceding window = 26 events immediately before the local window; preceding_stable_disagreement iff C2 >= 1 AND D2 * 2 > C2; long_disagreement iff stable_disagreement AND preceding_stable_disagreement). BRANCH AUTHORITY for the carried-over branches: ABSTENTION armed iff NOT stable_disagreement; RECOVERY armed iff NOT stable_disagreement OR recent_concordant_count >= 2 OR long_disagreement. The minority branch has its OWN arming condition (minority_fraction >= 0.25, below), which does not interact with this condition: the authority condition neither arms nor disarms the minority branch, and the minority fraction neither arms nor disarms recovery or abstention. Would-have-fired disarmed branches are recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire) and fall through. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters either condition.
fixed_parameters.minority_archive: THE SINGLE NEW ELEMENT OF THIS EXPERIMENT. Computed from the retained archive (events[:N-26]) and its own per-span majorities only. For each archive event e: let M(e) be the archive expectation for span(e) under the unchanged archive concordance definition (strictly-highest reported class among archive events of that span; tie or empty gives null). e is ARCHIVE-MATCHED if M(e) is progress or damage AND e's reported class is progress or damage (the same matched definition the concordance test applies to newest events, applied here to archive events against their own archive). e is MINORITY (discordant) if archive-matched AND e's reported class DIFFERS from M(e). The MINORITY SET is the set of all minority archive events, in chronological order. minority_matched_count = number of archive-matched archive events; minority_discordant_count = size of the minority set; minority_fraction = minority_discordant_count / minority_matched_count (0 if minority_matched_count == 0). All three counts and the fraction are recorded at every checkpoint. The minority set is not phase-segmented, receives no segment or switch information, and is recomputed from the archive exactly as the archive itself is.
fixed_parameters.minority_arming: The minority branch is ARMED iff minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8. The fraction threshold is fixed a priori from the simulator's known rates (see threshold_justification): pure-segment expectation 0.1625, +3.8 binomial sd at the B2-onset archive size; the count floor of 8 exists only so the branch is well-defined on short synthetic streams in unit tests and is never the binding constraint in evaluation (design minority_discordant_count at every graded checkpoint is >= 30). When the branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever the minority joint count says; a would-have-fired disarmed minority branch is recorded (minority_would_fire) and falls through.
fixed_parameters.minority_concordance_test: For each newest-window event e: the MINORITY EXPECTATION for span(e) is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among MINORITY-SET events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is MINORITY-MATCHED if its minority expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is MINORITY-CONCORDANT if minority-matched and its reported class EQUALS the minority expectation. minority_concordant_count and minority_matched_count (over the newest window) are in 0..2 and are recorded in full, with per-event minority records (span, reported class, minority-set count for the span, minority majority class or null, minority-matched flag, minority-concordant flag).
fixed_parameters.minority_joint_test: For each newest-window event e, e is MINORITY-JOINT if it is MINORITY-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference, unchanged) - both flags on the SAME event, mirroring the regular joint test with the concordance side read against the minority set instead of the whole archive. minority_joint_count in 0..2, recorded in full with per-event minority joint flags.
fixed_parameters.minority_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the MINORITY SET events only, with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose), exactly as the recovery model is fitted on the archive. The minority model never includes archive-concordant events, the reference window, or the newest window.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed (carried-over authority), act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive), exactly as the graded extended-reference candidate. (2) MINORITY RECOVERY - else if minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed (minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8), act through the minority model (source recorded as minority_archive). (3) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2 AND the abstention branch is armed, abstain (choose returns None), exactly as the graded candidates. (4) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch. The minority branch's position BELOW regular recovery is deliberate: at a first return both tests can in principle be evaluable, and the archive route - the one with five graded experiments of evidence - keeps precedence; the minority route is reserved for states the archive route cannot reach.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Every preceding cycle tested retained knowledge through the archive's global majority, and every protocol in the line pre-registered the same consequence: at the second switch that majority is the FIRST rule, so the retained B1 segment - the only retained knowledge that matches B2 - is invisible to a concordance test, because concordance was defined as agreement with that majority. This cycle keeps every definition and adds the complementary read of the same retained evidence: what the archive's events say AGAINST their own span majorities. That read is not a new signal source and not a threshold change: the discordant events were already computed (as the complement of concordant_count) and discarded in all five preceding experiments. The fraction arming is the cycle's selectivity mechanism, and it is an evidence summary, not a phase detector: it asks only whether the archive contains more disagreement than flip noise alone produces, a quantity with a known pure-segment expectation (0.1625) from the simulator's published rates. The design deliberately does NOT lower the abstention threshold to opposed_count >= 1: on stationary evidence a single opposed event occurs by flip noise in roughly 30 percent of newest-2 windows (1 - (1 - 0.1625)^2 over matched draws), so that change would abstain its way out of the control and release criteria - the graded guard's own records show opposed_count == 1 is the modal onset value at EVERY stage, switch or not. Protection at B2 must therefore come from a route that can distinguish a B2-following event from a flipped stationary event, and minority concordance is exactly that distinction in this simulator: a flipped stationary event reports the minority class on its span but is NOT opposed to a stationary reference, while a B2-following event is both minority-concordant and reference-opposed.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference candidate: the extended signal requires a 2-event newest window and a full 50-event reference window (at least 52 observed events); the archive concordance test requires at least 27. The minority computations require only the archive (at least 27 observed events) and are evaluable whenever the archive is; below 52 events the extended signal is not evaluable, minority_joint_count is recorded as 0 (its opposed side is not evaluable), and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable, gate_evaluable false). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so all windows are full and the fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, AND the full minority record - minority_matched_count, minority_discordant_count, minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, per-event minority concordance records, per-event minority joint flags, minority_joint_count, minority_would_fire flag - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates and the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). Composed disagreement rate 0.1625 (1/8 stochastic + 1/20 report flips), as in every preceding protocol in this line. (i) MINORITY ARMING THRESHOLD 0.25: under a single pure segment, an archive-matched non-neutral event is discordant with probability 0.1625, so minority_fraction concentrates at 0.1625 with binomial sd sqrt(0.1625 * 0.8375 / n); at the B2-onset archive (n ~ 260 matched non-neutral) sd ~ 0.023, so 0.25 is +3.8 sd - a pure or stationary stream crosses it with probability below 0.001 per checkpoint. With a real displaced segment of 64 events inside the archive the design fraction is ~0.31 (see hypothesis), about 2 sd above the threshold at the same n, so the branch is armed at B2 onset with design probability ~0.97 per state; at return-A onset the design fraction is ~0.26 (38 displaced events in the archive), so the branch may be armed there - by design, since its joint test is doubly blocked at a first return (hypothesis) and its return-A firing count is graded under criterion 1's selectivity sub-condition rather than assumed zero. At B1 onset and on the control arm the archive is single-segment and the design fraction is 0.1625, so the branch is unarmed there with probability above 0.999 per checkpoint. The count floor (minority_discordant_count >= 8) is a well-definedness guard for short streams only. (ii) MINORITY JOINT THRESHOLD minority_joint_count >= 1: carried over in FORM from the graded joint test (joint_count >= 1), the least sparse per-event test in the line; requiring 2 would square a per-event rate realized at ~0.56 design, repeating the retained-recovery experiment's graded failure (both-events concordance realized 1 of 6 engagement). (iii) All carried-over thresholds are UNCHANGED and not re-tuned: newest window 2, extended reference 50, legacy reference 24, archive events[:N-26], local window 26, preceding window 26, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention threshold opposed_count == 2, strict-majority rule D * 2 > C in both authority windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2. The only new fixed parameters are the minority fraction threshold (0.25) and its count floor (8), both derived above from the published noise rates and segment geometry (240 / 64 / 48 events), never from any score of this experiment.

expected_failure_modes: Information-empty B2 ceiling (pre-registered, structural): at B2 checkpoint 2 exactly 2 post-switch events exist, and in the graded extended-reference cohorts 2 of the 6 development B2 onset states (both at k=2) carried both-neutral newest draws. No newest-2 test - concordance, minority concordance, or opposition - can fire on draws with no class evidence, so B2 engagement can fail criterion 1's floor on an unlucky cohort even though the mechanism works as designed on informative draws. That outcome would show the B2 k=2 ceiling is set by newest-draw information, joining the return-A k=2 ceiling the extended-reference experiment established, and would redirect the next cycle toward a response that does not require an informative newest draw, under its own new protocol.

Abstention-conversion tradeoff at B2 (pre-registered, the cycle's central harm risk): on the graded additional cohort, abstention already protected B2 (candidate harm 15, guard 25, pooled). Minority recovery takes precedence over abstention wherever both could fire, so on such a cohort the branch converts zero-harm abstentions (0 successes) into minority-model play (design ~10-13 successes at ~3-6 harmful actions per state). B2 pooled harm can therefore RISE from the extended baseline's level toward ~25-35 and fail criterion 1's harm sub-condition (at or below the guard) even while B2 successes rise by 40+. That outcome is informative - it would show B2 protection and B2 productivity are in direct tradeoff through this route - and is charged against criterion 1, not excused.

Minority fraction realization below the arming threshold: the design fraction at B2 onset is ~0.31 with binomial sd ~0.03, but a cohort whose B1 segment produced fewer archive-discordant reports (more neutral draws, more double flips) can realize 0.23-0.24, leaving the branch unarmed at some or all B2 states. The candidate then behaves identically to the graded extended-reference baseline at those states - a null result that the recorded minority_fraction values make fully distinguishable from a joint-test failure (fraction recorded at every checkpoint; criterion 1's report must state the realized fractions).

Minority model quality - the flip-symmetry limit (stated, bounded): the minority pool's per-span majorities describe the inverted rule in this simulator partly because flips are exact progress/damage inversions, so original-segment flip reports reinforce the inverted class instead of diluting it. In a world whose second rule were not an exact inversion, or whose noise were not class-flipping, the minority pool would be noise and the minority model worthless. Within this simulator the design inverted share is ~0.80 per span, but if the realized share lands lower (thin spans, tie majorities giving null minority expectations), minority concordance coverage falls, engagement drops toward the floor, and minority-model play harm rises toward recent8 levels - failing criterion 1 on either sub-condition. The claim, if it passes, is bounded accordingly in the grading definitions: this is a designer-supplied read of retained discordant evidence in an inversion simulator, not a general displaced-segment discovery mechanism.

False minority engagement at B1 late checkpoints or return-A: at B1 checkpoint 32 the archive begins to include the first B1 events (design fraction ~0.22, within sampling distance of 0.25), and at return-A the branch may be armed by design (~0.26). The joint test is argued to block both (B1 late: newest events follow the current inverted rule and the reference is segment-pure inverted by k=32, so they are not reference-opposed; return-A: doubly blocked per the hypothesis), but a flipped newest event can in principle satisfy minority concordance plus opposition spuriously (a flipped current-rule event reports the displaced class and opposes the current reference). Criterion 1 grades minority firing at B1 and return-A onset (at most 1 of 6 each), criterion 6 grades the checkpoint-32 records, and persistence at checkpoints 8/16 is reported.

Minority persistence at checkpoints 8 and 16 at B2: while the extended reference still describes the returned segment (until k ~ 50), minority recovery can keep firing deep into B2, which is productive while the minority model is right but delays recent8's own adaptation from taking over; at checkpoint 32 the reference is segment-pure B2, so minority-joint requires a flipped newest event - design rare - and release is graded under criterion 6 including its records sub-condition, which counts minority_archive among the non-recent8 branches.

Return-A profile interaction: the minority branch sits below regular recovery and above abstention, so at a return-A state where regular recovery does not fire but a spurious minority-joint event occurs (design: requires a flipped or discordant newest draw satisfying both flags - argued doubly blocked, but the argument rests on majority correctness on both sides), the learner would play the minority (intervening-rule) model at a return, costing return-A successes and harm. Criteria 2 and 4 grade the return-A profile against the graded extended-reference levels, and the minority firing count at return-A is reported from records at every checkpoint, not only onset.

baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and the candidate's own acting model: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.
baselines.in: all criteria comparisons as named; every candidate-vs-recent8 difference is attributable to the decision rule (now including its minority branch) alone

baselines.name: extended_reference_joint_recovery
baselines.role: ExtendedReferenceJointRecoveryMemory, the preceding experiment's candidate (graded Partially demonstrated): identical acting model, identical extended signal, identical archive and concordance definitions, identical joint test, identical recovery model, identical abstention trigger, and the identical three-leg authority condition, differing ONLY in that it has no minority branch. This is the decisive comparison for this experiment: candidate-vs-extended-candidate differences isolate the minority branch alone, at B2 above all (criterion 1), and at return-A and checkpoint 32 (criteria 2, 4, 6).
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1-6 comparisons in the report (its totals are the decisive branch comparison, not PASS/FAIL comparators beyond the criteria as named)

baselines.name: evidence_opposition_guard
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory (graded Demonstrated): the 24-event-reference signal and acting model, with abstention as its only protective response. Criteria 1, 3, and 4 hold the candidate to the guard's harm levels on the same cohort - at B2 (criterion 1) the guard is the ONLY preceding method that ever protected the second switch on a development-type cohort (78 vs recent8 94, via a single abstention firing).
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1, 3, and 4 comparisons

baselines.name: long_disagreement_joint_recovery
baselines.role: LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): the 24-event-reference predecessor with the full authority condition.

baselines.role: BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): the two-leg authority predecessor.
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; checkpoint-32 comparisons in the report

baselines.name: joint_concordance_recovery
baselines.role: JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): the unexpired joint candidate with the 24-event reference.

baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events. Plain cumulative retention remains the strongest simple retained comparator at return-A and is reported in full there; at B2 it is original-dominated (0 successes / 96 harm on the graded development cohort) and is the standing proof that undifferentiated retention cannot protect the second switch.

baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, the pooled both-events candidate (graded Failed): the engagement-sparsity reference point.

acceptance_criteria.name: second_switch_B2_protection_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded extended-reference candidate failed pooled onset harm on development entirely at B2 (94 = recent8 vs guard 78; no branch fired in any B2 onset state on that cohort, recovery 0 of 6 on both cohorts). Graded per cohort over the B2 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the minority recovery branch is TAKEN (minority_joint_count >= 1, minority branch armed, acting source minority_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B2 onset seed-checkpoint states - the low edge of this protocol's unconditional design interval of approx 4-5 of 6 after the pre-registered information-empty share, as derived in threshold_justification; AND (b) SELECTIVITY - the minority recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states AND at most 1 of the 6 pooled return-A onset states on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B2 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort (the selected limitation's measurable form, carried exactly), AND candidate B2 pooled onset harm <= 0.60 * recent8 B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort; AND (d) PRODUCTIVITY - candidate successes pooled over the B2 onset cells >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16. Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized minority_fraction and minority_armed flag at each, and against the records-only extended-rule derivation (see metrics_reported), so the report distinguishes minority engagement from states the preceding candidate would have taken anyway (by construction the extended rule takes NO B2 onset state via recovery, and its abstention firings at B2 are reported alongside for the conversion tradeoff). Abstention-branch firing at B2 is reported but does NOT count toward sub-condition (a): the preceding experiments establish that abstention alone, where it fires at all, is the cohort-lucky protection this cycle exists to replace with a retained-knowledge response.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). Cumulative's, the joint candidate's, the bounded candidate's, the long candidate's, and the extended candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. The minority branch must not give back the first-return profile the extended candidate graded PASS on both cohorts (44 / 62 successes against these same floors).

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint, bounded, long, and extended protocols. This is the criterion the graded extended candidate FAILed on development (192 vs guard 182, the entire margin at B2); criterion 1 grades the B2 repair directly and this criterion grades that the repair, plus the rest of the onset profile, brings the pooled figure to the guard's level. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. Carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols; the graded extended candidate PASSed it on both cohorts (52 vs guard 58 and ceiling 54.0; 34 vs guard 45 and ceiling 49.2) and this cycle must not give it back through any minority-branch interference at the first return.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (carried over unchanged), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive, minority_archive, or abstained) in at most 1 state - the direct records-level measure that every gate in the candidate, including the new minority branch, has actually released late. Carried over from the extended protocol with the minority branch added to the counted branches.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_downstream_selectivity
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. Identical in form to the preceding protocols' stationary criterion. The realized minority_fraction and minority_armed values on the control arm are recorded and reported at every checkpoint (design: fraction at the pure flip-noise level 0.1625, branch unarmed throughout); the downstream totals are what is graded here, and any control checkpoint at which the minority branch was armed is stated explicitly in the report.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, AND the full minority record: minority_matched_count, minority_discordant_count, minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, per-event minority concordance records, per-event minority joint flags, minority_joint_count, minority_would_fire flag, branch taken, recovery-fired flag, minority-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 1(c): candidate B2 pooled onset harm at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's B2 pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's B2 pooled onset harm. Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the guard's pooled onset harm on the same cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The abstention-conversion tradeoff at B2 (expected failure mode 2) is charged against criterion 1(c), not excused from it.
budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the preceding protocols. Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the carried-over release mechanism, not a budget violation.

metrics_reported: Per seed, per stage (B1, return_A, B2, control), per checkpoint, per method: successes, harmful TEST actions, failed-by-abstention count, attempted tasks.

Candidate decision record at every checkpoint, per seed: the EXTENDED-reference signal record and the LEGACY reference-24 signal record exactly as in the graded extended-reference protocol (records-only for the legacy record), the archive concordance record exactly as in the graded retained-recovery protocol, the per-event JOINT flag and joint_count under the extended reference, the AUTHORITY record exactly as in the graded long / extended protocols (local and preceding span records, comparable/disagreeing counts, stable and preceding-stable flags, long_disagreement flag, recent_concordant_count, recovery arming leg, per-branch armed and would-fire flags), AND the MINORITY record (minority_matched_count and minority_discordant_count over the archive, minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, minority_would_fire flag, per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, minority-set event count for that span, minority majority class or null, minority-matched flag, minority-concordant flag, minority joint flag; plus minority_concordant_count, minority_matched_count over the newest window, and minority_joint_count), the branch taken (retained_archive / minority_archive / abstained / recent8 / all_available_below_minimum), recovery-fired flag, minority-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, and the acting source.

Engagement aggregates per cohort, from the decision records alone: recovery-fired states, minority-fired states, abstention states, recent8 states, and - separately - recovery-would-fire-but-disarmed, minority-would-fire-but-disarmed, and abstention-would-fire-but-disarmed states, among the 6 pooled B2 onset states (reported ALSO split checkpoint 2 alone vs checkpoint 4 alone, as criterion 1's population), the 6 pooled return-A onset states, the 6 pooled B1 onset states, the graded control states, and the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states; minority states reported with their realized minority_fraction values; recovery states split by arming leg (no stable disagreement / corroboration / long disagreement); PLUS, for continuity with every preceding experiment, the states at which the graded extended candidate's rule (extended joint_count / opposed_count with the same authority condition, no minority branch), the graded long candidate's rule (legacy reference-24 counts with the same authority), the graded bounded candidate's authority (no long leg), and the graded joint candidate's unexpired rule would have taken a non-recent8 branch, all computed from this candidate's recorded counts and flags (all underlying counts are recorded in full, so these are records-only derivations, not re-runs). The B2 split of the extended derivation is reported alongside, so the minority branch's B2 effect is graded from the records alone.
Onset harm and successes at checkpoint 0 for every stage, per seed and method, reported explicitly as a diagnostic and never pooled into any graded onset figure and never hidden.

Persistence cost: candidate abstentions, recovery engagements, minority engagements, would-fire-but-disarmed counts (all three branches), successes, and harm at checkpoints 8 and 16 per stage, reported alongside the checkpoint-32 release figures, with the realized minority_fraction trajectory per stage stated explicitly.
Per seed TRAIN accounting, counted once regardless of checkpoints or methods: actor actions, actual harmful actions, actual productive, actual neutral, reported harmful, report label flips.
Learner-issued information-acquisition actions (frozen at 0) and any additional observations requested (frozen at 0).
Checkpoint record SHA256 and restore-replay identity for the candidate.
No pooled-only reporting: every cohort figure must be decomposable into its three per-seed rows, and every pooled criterion figure into its per-cell rows.
required_evaluation_runs: This experiment's frozen benchmark on the development cohort and on the additional cohort, exactly as registered here.
Full unit suite: python -m unittest discover -s tests

grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary. Criterion 1 is reported first among the criteria in the grading report, as this experiment's primary criterion (its engagement sub-condition (a) first within it, then selectivity (b), harm (c), and productivity (d)); criteria 4 and 5 (return-A harm and release) are reported next, as its co-graded guards.
grading.demonstrated: All seven criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit.
grading.failed: Criterion 1 FAILs on the additional cohort, or any of criteria 2, 3, 4, or 5 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criterion 1 and criterion 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the candidate's checkpoint-32 successes fall below the graded extended candidate's checkpoint-32 deficit pattern (i.e. below recent8 - 4 on either cohort, the extended candidate's worse cohort gap), or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, minority, routing, expiry, disagreement-age, and reference-width rules). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, joint tests, minority definition and arming threshold, disagreement / corroboration / long-disagreement conditions, and the decision rule are all designer-supplied, and the minority read exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (see expected failure mode 4). A PASS would demonstrate minority-evidence recovery - protection of a second switch from retained discordant evidence that a global-majority concordance test structurally discards - in this simulator only, not general displaced-segment discovery, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled return-A or B2 onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 3 per stage per cohort at checkpoint 2 alone, 6 per stage per cohort pooled at checkpoints 2 and 4, and 9 switch-stage states per cohort at checkpoint 32.
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the nine graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_retained_recovery, joint_concordance_recovery, bounded_authority_joint_recovery, long_disagreement_joint_recovery, extended_reference_joint_recovery, and the abstention guard counted once) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the acting model, the extended and legacy references, the retained archive, the archive concordance definition, the joint recovery test's form, the recovery model, the abstention trigger's form and threshold, the local-archive disagreement definition, the corroboration condition, and the long-disagreement leg are reused EXACTLY as frozen in the extended-reference protocol (newest window 2, reference 50 / legacy 24, archive events[:N-26], local window last 26, preceding window 26 before it, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention threshold opposed_count == 2, stable_disagreement iff C >= 1 AND D * 2 > C in both windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2). The single new element - the minority archive set, its concordance and joint tests in the same per-event form, its model fitted on the minority set only, and its arming condition (minority_fraction >= 0.25 with a count floor of 8) - is informed only by the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records (their limitation evidence, including the per-state B2 record decomposition in limitation_evidence), the simulator's known noise rates, and this simulator's published segment geometry (240 / 64 / 48 events), never by any score of this experiment (none exist).
